title: Glaw a haul: weather and the hills
intro: Living under Yr Wyddfa, you learn the weather words first.
Mostly the one for rain. Shall we?

words.note: Rhymes with 'cow'. Mae hi'n bwrw glaw: it's raining (literally 'it's throwing rain').
Rhymes with 'while'. Rarer round here than glaw.
Said quickly, almost one syllable.
dd is the 'th' in 'this'. Most Welsh words stress the last syllable but one.
A single f is said 'v'. Two of them, ff, is the English 'f'.
The little hat (to bach) makes the vowel long.

tip: Mae hi'n braf means 'it's fine weather'. Worth knowing, if only to say it once a year.

title: Paned? The caffi and the tafarn
intro: In Wales, nothing gets sorted without a paned first.
Learn these and you'll never go thirsty.

words.note: Short for cwpanaid, 'a cupful'. In the North it's often panad.
ll: tongue behind your top teeth as for 'l', then blow out past its sides. ae sounds like 'eye'. In the North: llefrith (LLEV-rith).
The dried fruit is soaked overnight in tea. Lovely buttered.
w is a vowel in Welsh, the 'oo' in 'pool'. Roll the r.
ch is the throaty sound in 'loch', never the 'ch' in 'chips'.
Ga i baned? The p of paned softens to b after it. More on that in the mutation lesson.

tip: Ga i baned, os gwelwch yn dda? is a whole polite order: may I have a cuppa, please?

title: Aber, llan, pen: reading the map
intro: Most place names in Wales are little descriptions, if you know the pieces.
Learn eight and the map starts talking to you.

words.note: Aberystwyth sits at the mouth of the Ystwyth. Swansea is Abertawe, the mouth of the Tawe.
Usually followed by a saint: Llanberis is Peris's, Llangollen is Collen's (the first letter softens).
Pen y Fan, the highest peak in Bannau Brycheiniog (the Brecon Beacons).
Caerdydd is Cardiff. Holyhead is Caergybi, Cybi's fort.
Treorci (Treorchy), up the Rhondda. Careful: not every Tre- is a town. Trefor, in the Dee valley, is a personal name.
Nant Ffrancon, the valley below Ogwen.

Pontypridd grew up around its old stone bridge over the Taf. Pontcysyllte, the aqueduct near Trevor, is pont + cysyllte, 'the joining'. Pont y Borth (also Pont Grog y Borth) is the Menai Suspension Bridge to Anglesey.
Betws-y-Coed: the prayer house in the wood.

tip: Describing words come after the noun: Llyn Mawr is 'lake big', a big lake.

title: Gath, not cath: the soft mutation
intro: Welsh words change their first letter after certain little words. It's called mutation.
Sounds scary. It's really just making things easier to say.

words.note: After ei meaning 'his', c softens to g. In the North: ei gath o.
y sounds like the 'u' in 'fun' in most syllables, and like 'i' in the last one.
After i ('to'), C softens to G. Croeso i Gymru: welcome to Wales.
M softens to F, which is said 'v'. Croeso i Ferthyr!
Dw i'n hoffi coffi: I like coffee. In the North you'll hear dw i'n licio (LIK-yo) as well.
dd is the 'th' in 'this'.

tip: The soft mutation: c to g, p to b, t to d, b and m to f, d to dd, ll to l, rh to r, and g just drops off. Forget it and you'll still be understood.
